overview: The Genesee–Vanderbilt was a combined Red Mountain mine complex between the Yankee Girl and National Belle properties.

Local district chronology records the Genesee as located in summer 1882 and the neighboring Vanderbilt in 1883; the Genesee interests acquired the Vanderbilt in 1888, and the workings were combined by early 1889 after the two mines were recognized as developing the same ore body.

moreHistory: USGS Bulletin 182 provides the contemporary technical and mapping anchor for the Silverton–Red Mountain mining landscape.
Historic ore was principally silver-bearing galena, while later locality records also associate the complex with copper, zinc, lead, gold, and silver.
District sources record renewed activity after the late-1890s revival, but the exact shutdown sequence and lifetime production remain uncertain and no aggregate total is adopted.

Surviving identification features include large dumps, ore-loading or tram-related remnants, deteriorated buildings, and the disturbed high-alpine mine landscape; uncertain structure functions should remain qualified.

Component safeguard: keep the original Genesee and Vanderbilt workings, their later combined system, the Joker Tunnel/Idarado connection, Guston townsite, Yankee Girl, and Guston–Robinson as separate linked elements.
